documents.title: Ferroptosis-related endothelial protection by Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury: network pharmacology and validation in endothelial cells.
documents.abstract: Ischemic stroke and ischemic acute kidney injury are both clinical challenges. Danhong injection (DHI) has been reported to exert protective effects against cerebral and renal ischemic injury. However, the shared therapeutic targets and mechanisms underlying its effects in these two organs remain unclear. Using network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro experiments, this study investigated shared targets and pathways associated with cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and evaluated whether DHI exerted a shared ferroptosis-related endot

documents.title: Efficient flavonoids from Helichrysum bracteatum and their multi-target antioxidant mechanisms.
documents.abstract: Helichrysum bracteatum is a promising source of natural antioxidants for food preservation. However, unclear mechanisms and inefficient extraction limit the application of its flavonoids in functional foods. Here, we report a response surface methodology (RSM)-optimized hydroethanolic reflux extraction yielding a maximum flavonoid extraction yield of 16.0% under optimized conditions (27: 1 mL/g, 68% ethanol, 1.6 h). The major flavonoids identified were quercetin (29.44%), kaempferol (8.03%), and rutin (3.44%), and the extract exhibited strong radical-scavenging activity. Network analysis ident

documents.title: Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing.
documents.abstract: Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have been widely used for mRNA delivery, understanding how cholesterol analogues modulate LNP properties and intracellular trafficking to enhance transfection efficiency remains essential for the rational design of next-generation delivery systems. This study investigated their structure-activity relationships and effects on mRNA delivery. We hypothesized that C-24 alkyl-substituted phytosterols enhance transfection by modulating LNP physicochemical properties and interactions with intracellular transport proteins. These phytosterols altered LNP mechanics an

documents.title: Mechanisms of Hofmeister ion effects on protein properties and their applications in food protein processing: A review.
documents.abstract: The Hofmeister series is a fundamental paradigm for ion-specific regulation of protein properties, with anions playing a dominant role. However, its molecular mechanism remains long-debated, and a systematic synthesis linking basic theory to food protein processing practices is still lacking. This review dissects the action mechanisms of Hofmeister anions from water structure regulation and ion-protein interactions, and summarizes their applications in protein extraction, gelation, emulsion stabilization and structural modification. The principal finding is that the Hofmeister effect arises fr

documents.title: Structure-based binding pocket conservation analysis identifies 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase candidates across phylogenetically diverse bacteria.
documents.abstract: Urolithins are polyphenolic compounds produced by gut microbiota from dietary ellagitannins and ellagic acid, with urolithin A being the most bioactive and associated with a range of pharmaceutical activities like anti-aging and anti-inflammatory effects. Despite these benefits, the number of known urolithin A-producing bacteria and their corresponding enzymes is very limited. In this study, we combined conventional sequence-based homology search with structural modeling to identify novel bacteria potentially harboring 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylases, primarily characterized in the Enterocloster

documents.title: AlphaFold models of host-pathogen interactions elucidate the prevalence and structural modes of molecular mimicry.
documents.abstract: Pathogens exploit host cellular machinery through protein-protein interactions (PPIs), often using molecular mimicry to hijack host cellular processes. While there have been thousands of host-pathogen PPIs determined to date, the lack of structural information for these impedes the study of the prevalence of molecular mimicry and convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. To address this, we benchmarked AlphaFold2 and 3 for prediction of structures of host-pathogen interactions observing that accurate models can be retrieved when ranking by modelling confidence, despite an overall

documents.title: Large-scale analysis of AlphaFold structures reveals organism-specific physicochemical signatures.
documents.abstract: Recent advancements in protein structure prediction methods have ushered in a new era of abundant and accurate structural data, providing opportunities to analyse proteins at a scale that has not been possible before. Here we performed a large-scale analysis of physicochemical properties across 373,779 confident AlphaFold structures. Our analysis revealed systematic variation between proteins from different organisms to such an extent that major features of the tree of life could be recovered from these data. Surprisingly, this relationship persisted even when we restricted our analysis to euk

documents.title: Effect of amino acid substitutions on the structure and dynamics of human PRPP synthetase PRPS1.
documents.abstract: Phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP), is required for the synthesis of nucleotides and mutations in human PRPP synthetase (hPRPS1) are linked to Arts syndrome and X-linked Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 5. Here, we investigated mutations linked to these neurological diseases using molecular dynamics simulations. We highlight small but measurable correlations between structural change and kinetic properties as demonstrated by mutant A190V, which exhibits reduced feedback inhibition by ADP and GDP, consistent with superactivity of PRPS1. Changes in RMSD and Rg indicate increased flexibility of mutant Q1

documents.title: Predicting Asymmetric Organocatalysis via Machine-Learning-Driven Molecular Dynamics of Chiral Deep Eutectic Solvents.
documents.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) serve as sustainable, low-volatility, and bio-derived alternatives to conventional organic media, aligning with the demand for green chemical processes. Beyond their role as solvents, they offer transformative potential as integrated catalytic platforms, yet the molecular determinants of their performance remain poorly understood. This study employs machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics combined with density functional theory to investigate the structure and dynamics of chiral deep eutectic solvents in asymmetric catalysis. Simulations reveal that overly pers

documents.title: Network pharmacology and molecular dynamics uncover RMJ's targets and mechanisms for treating atherosclerosis.
documents.abstract: Atherosclerosis involves complex pathogenesis including inflammation, lipid disorders, and abnormal autophagy, yet current treatments are limited by adverse reactions and drug resistance, highlighting the need for novel strategies.

documents.title: AARS1-Mediated GLUD1 K503 Lactylation Drives Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through Post-Transcriptional Reprogramming.
documents.abstract: The prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) largely depends on whether metastasis occurs. The Warburg effect leads to lactate accumulation and potential lysine lactylation (Kla), thereby promoting tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of non-histone Kla in CRC metastasis remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases (LM) and paired primary tumors (PT) from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), together with multi-omics analyses and in vitro and in vivo validation, identified GLUD1 as a key lactyla

documents.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled natural product pharmacology: From molecular discovery to precision therapeutics.
documents.abstract: The use of natural products as a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules for drug development has been well established; however, their multicomponent and multitarget nature, uncertain target causality, variable in vivo exposure, and heterogeneous responses to therapy make them challenging to characterize pharmacologically and translate into clinical practice. Systems pharmacology, together with artificial intelligence (AI), provides new approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, integration of multidimensional data, and development of precision therapeutics. documents.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
documents.abstract: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant.

documents.title: Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields.
documents.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) has become a cornerstone of structure-based drug design, yet its success has been built almost entirely on protein targets. Extending this physical rigor to RNA─an emerging and largely untapped therapeutic target class─confronts challenges that protein-ligand systems rarely impose: pronounced conformational flexibility, dense and highly anisotropic electrostatics, and ligand binding that frequently depends on direct metal coordination. documents.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation

documents.title: Enhancing Enzyme pH Adaptation for Industrial Biocatalysis: From Sequence-Dependent Engineering to Sequence-Independent Stabilization.
documents.abstract: Enzymes are indispensable biocatalysts in industrial processes, but their application is often restricted by narrow pH optima. Exposure to acidic or alkaline conditions alters the protonation states of ionizable residues, disrupts catalytic microenvironments and stabilizing interactions, and ultimately reduces activity, catalytic efficiency, or structural integrity. This limitation is particularly important in industrial sectors such as detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutic formulations, where operation under non-native pH conditions is frequently required. Conventional sequence

documents.title: CovPDB 2.0: an expanded covalent protein-ligand interactome.
documents.abstract: The rational design of covalently binding inhibitors to specifically block selected target proteins has become a common strategy in drug discovery. Such design is based on structural insights into how electrophilic ligands bind to nucleophilic residues. CovPDB v1.0 provided high-resolution cocrystal structures of biologically relevant covalent protein-ligand complexes curated from the Protein Data Bank. Here, we describe CovPDB v2.0, a substantially extended release that addresses three main limitations of the original resource. First, to reflect the numerous novel covalently binding ligands d

documents.title: Integrating artificial intelligence prescreening with molecular dynamics for the design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors as promising therapeutic agents against breast cancer, including the triple-negative subtype.
documents.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Notably, published studies have shown that the WWP1 enzyme plays a pivotal role in driving PTEN degradation via ubiquitination, identifying it as a promising therap

documents.title: Conformational Plasticity of Orthosteric Pocket Enables the Discovery of a Novel PAD4-Selective Inhibitor.
documents.abstract: Peptidyl-arginine deiminase (PAD) family enzymes are pivotal enzymes that catalyze the citrullination of arginine in substrate proteins. Elevated levels of citrullinated proteins are tightly linked to the incidence of rheumatoid arthritis, neurodegenerative diseases, and cancers, thus highlighting PAD enzymes as important therapeutic targets. Although several PAD isozyme-selective and non-selective small molecule inhibitors have been reported over the last decade, it remains important to identify distinct ligands that may offer differentiated therapeutic potential or selectivity. Herein, we pr

documents.title: Nanomaterial-based glucose sensors: detection platforms and highlight applications.
documents.abstract: Glucose acts as a fundamental energy substrate sustaining human physiological homeostasis, and aberrant blood glucose levels are tightly correlated with a spectrum of metabolic disorders, particularly diabetes mellitus, which has evolved into a severe global public health crisis. Precise, rapid, and stable glucose monitoring is therefore indispensable for the early diagnosis, clinical intervention, and long-term management of diabetes. Conventional enzyme-dependent glucose sensors suffer from inherent limitations, including high manufacturing costs, inferior environmental stability, short serv

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing.
documents.abstract: Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that OH- forms strong chemical bonds with surface Zr atoms, thereby inducing surface hydroxylation and increasing the

documents.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
documents.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. This

documents.title: Computational Structural and Dynamic Insights into the Proposed TcP21-CXCR4 Interaction: A Consensus-Based Multireplica Simulation Approach.
documents.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need for novel targeted strategies. The parasite's secreted 21 kDa virulence factor, TcP21, promotes extracellular amastigote host-cell invasion and persistence by interacting with the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a class A G protein-coupled receptor. Despite its biological importance, the structural determinants governing TcP21-CXCR4 complex formation remain unknown. To elucidate the molecular basis of this host-parasite recognition, multiple initial candidate bin

documents.title: Integrated Toxicological, Network Toxicology, and Molecular Simulation Assessment of Inhalation Toxicity and Mechanisms of HFO-1336mzz(E) as an SF6 Alternative Insulating Gas.
documents.abstract: HFO-1336mzz-(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. To address this issue, the present study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the biological safety of HFO-1336mzz-(E) by integrating multilevel toxicological assessment with molecular mechanistic analysis. Acute inhal

documents.title: Investigating Ferritin Permeability to Metal-Based Drugs through Molecular Dynamics.
documents.abstract: In this study, we implemented a workflow based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to assess whether gold-(I)-containing complexes can traverse the C3 channels of human H ferritin and which energetic barriers were at play in the process. By using two example complexes for which an extensive experimental characterization was already available, we observed that classical MD correctly indicated which one could spontaneously pass through the channel. documents.title: Solving the Computational Peptide Design Puzzle: Challenges and Opportunities.
documents.abstract: Peptides are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutics, antimicrobial agents, and supramolecular biomaterials due to the remarkable versatility encoded in their amino acid sequences. However, the rational design of peptides remains challenging because sequence-structure-function relationships are not yet fully understood. Experimental exploration of peptide chemical space is inherently limited by the vast number of possible sequences and the complexity of resolving peptide behavior at molecular resolution. Computational methods, particularly molecular dynamics simulations and, more rec

documents.title: Structural Characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis IspQ Reveals Membrane-Dependent Stabilization of Its Conserved Electron-Transfer Cofactor Network.
documents.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence in granulomas depends on lipid catabolism through the β-oxidation-coupled respiratory pathway, which requires the essential membrane-associated protein IspQ, encoded by Rv0338c. Although IspQ is a genetically and chemically validated drug target, its structural organization and membrane-dependent function remain unknown. Using AlphaFold3 structure prediction, cofactor mapping, evolutionary conservation analysis, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we show that IspQ adopts an EtfD-like fold containing four iron-sulfur clusters, a heme b, and a me

documents.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO2/CH4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes.
documents.abstract: Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. documents.title: Flexible Receptor Docking Provides Structural Models for the Recognition of 2‑Amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide Derivatives by Lck via the CorrEA Method.
documents.abstract: Structural models of Lck bound to a chemically diverse series of 62 2-amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide (AHBA) inhibitors were built to examine how the conformational state of the ATP-binding site shapes the structure-based interpretation of their potency. Docking to the static Lck crystal structure (PDB entry 1QPC) generated plausible complexes for only 54 of the 62 compounds, and produced essentially no relationship between docking scores and experimental pIC50 values, indicating that a single receptor conformation cannot capture how this scaffold is recognized. documents.title: Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.
documents.abstract: The global dissemination of subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), especially New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase-2 (VIM-2), and imipenemase-1 (IMP-1), threatens the clinical utility of carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics. This challenge is compounded by the absence of any commercially available MBL inhibitors for clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for novel inhibitor development. Computational approaches now guide much of MBL inhibitor discovery, yet many compounds predicted to bind B1 MBLs, or even shown to inhibit purified en

documents.title: Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network.
documents.abstract: Photosystem II (PSII) contains a diverse array of pigment-protein subunits with specialized roles in the antenna network. We investigate the functional significance of this subunit diversity in two structurally similar yet functionally distinct PSII subunits: minor light-harvesting complex CP29 and major light-harvesting complex LHCII. We combine two-dimensional electronic-vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling to assign spectral features to exciton states, providing molecular detail to probed spectral features. We show how the distinct pig
documents.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters

documents.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
documents.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium (TPANIC), with the goal of providing

documents.title: Structure-based discovery of new GPR119 ligands from on-demand tera-scale chemical space.
documents.abstract: The orphan G protein-coupled receptor GPR119 is involved in glucose homeostasis and is considered a promising target for the treatment of diabetes and other metabolic diseases. The recently solved structures of GPR119 in complex with potential endogenous lipid agonists, including oleoylethanolamide (OEA), provide a solid platform for 3D pharmacology analysis and structure-based ligand discovery. Here, we employed the V-SYNTHES2 approach to screen ∼3 trillion on-demand compounds from Enamine xREAL chemical space to identify several new chemotypes of GPR119 agonists and antagonists. Structure-gu
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES.
documents.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Structure-Based Discovery of GTP-Enhanced Rab10 Modulators and Their Effects on Alzheimer's Disease-Relevant Cellular Phenotypes.
documents.abstract: Rab10-mediated membrane trafficking has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but pharmacological tools for investigating its function remain limited. Here, we screened more than 80 million compounds using structure-based virtual screening and prioritized five candidate Rab10 modulators ( R1-R5 ). These compounds exhibited favorable docking scores, stable modeled protein-ligand complexes in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and predicted acceptable ADME/toxicity profiles. Comparative docking against Rab5, Rab8, and Rab11 predicted preferential interactions with GTP-associated Rab10. R
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Large-Scale Prospective Virtual Screening Using a Co-Folding-Rescoring Workflow for NPM1-TYK2 Inhibitor Discovery.
documents.abstract: Conventional large-scale structure-based virtual screening typically relies on fixed-receptor docking, in which ligand poses are sampled against a predefined receptor conformation. Protein-ligand co-folding models can instead generate candidate complex conformations by jointly modeling ligand placement and local receptor-ligand structural adaptation. documents.title: Synthesis and Evaluation of Novel Derivatives of 3,4,5-Trisubstituted Triazole as Potential Cyclooxygenase Inhibitors.
documents.abstract: The series of [2-[(5-(4-aminophenyl)-4-phenyl-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio]-N-(thiazol-2-yl)]acetamide derivatives (C1-C12) were designed, synthesized, evaluated in vitro against the cyclooxygenase enzymes COX-1 and COX-2, and characterized by HRMS, 1H-NMR, and 13C-NMR spectroscopy. The series displayed a diverse inhibition profile: C7 and C9 emerged as potent dual COX-1/COX-2 inhibitors, with C7 being the most active COX-2 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.308 ± 0.014 μM), whereas C3 and C6 acted as highly COX-1-selective inhibitors (IC50 = 0.083 and 0.096 μM, respectively), and C10 showed a COX-2-selective

documents.title: Immunoinformatic and Structural Design of an Influenza A DNA Vaccine Based on Conserved Nucleoprotein Epitopes and Heat Shock Protein 70 Adjuvant.
documents.abstract: Influenza A is a health concern, as it constantly mutates and changes antigens. The conventional vaccine is not very effective in providing immunity. We have designed and characterized a DNA multi-epitope vaccine based on conserved regions of the influenza A nucleoprotein (NP) and have assessed the immune response.

documents.title: Diversity at the Acinetobacter baumannii K locus: towards a comprehensive database for in silico prediction of capsular polysaccharide types.
documents.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is one of the most critical bacterial pathogens requiring novel approaches for infection control and treatment to curb the spread of highly resistant isolates. Epidemiological surveillance and the design and application of many non-antibiotic interventions require rapid and accurate prediction of diverse capsular polysaccharide (CPS) types from whole-genome sequence data. The internationally adopted CPS typing system relies on the in silico detection of CPS biosynthesis genes both in and outside the K locus (KL), utilizing a reference sequence database that is compatibl

documents.title: Structural Determinants of Biologic Recognition Across GPCR Classes.
documents.abstract: The rapid increase in experimentally resolved G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-biologic complexes has substantially improved our understanding of the molecular basis of receptor recognition and modulation. However, despite the growing number of available structures, a comparative framework integrating the major GPCR classes is still lacking. In this review, we analysed experimentally resolved GPCR-biologic complexes across receptor Classes A, B, C, and F to identify the structural principles governing biologic recognition. Our analysis shows that the architecture of each GPCR class shapes dis

documents.title: Aggregate-associated interfacial organization of sodium oleate near zircon surfaces.
documents.abstract: Sodium oleate (NaOL) is widely used as an anionic collector for zircon flotation, yet its heterogeneous organization at zircon surfaces remains insufficiently characterized.

documents.title: Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics-Based Investigation of the Potential Anti-Inflammatory and Cell-Survival Regulatory Mechanisms of Dapansutrile in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
documents.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterised by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive cartilage and bone destruction, and disability. Existing therapies can be limited by adverse effects and cost, and additional treatment approaches remain of interest. Dapansutrile (OLT1177) is an orally active, selective inhibitor of the NLRP3 inflammasome that has shown anti-inflammatory activity and good tolerability in early clinical studies. Whether dapansutrile might also interact with other RA-related proteins has not been examined specifically in RA. This study used c
documents.journal: Open access rheumatology : research and reviews

documents.title: AI-driven strategies for Cas12 protein design and genome editing optimization.
documents.abstract: The rise of the CRISPR-CAS system has greatly promoted the development of gene editing technology. Cas12, with its unique molecular characteristics, has become an important editing tool following Cas9. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in Cas12-related research, ranging from protein structure optimization, target design to editing efficiency prediction and off-target risk assessment. AI has demonstrated great potential in enhancing system performance and discovering new mutants. Most of these models were trained and benchmarked in human cell lines, E. coli,

documents.title: Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 promotes dermal papilla cell proliferation and modulates wnt/ β  -catenin signaling and androgen receptor conformational dynamics.
documents.abstract: Dermal papilla cells regulate hair follicle growth, yet bioactive peptides that influence both pro-growth signaling and androgen receptor (AR)-associated regulation remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the effects of Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 (MT12) on human dermal papilla cell function and its potential interaction with the AR ligand-binding domain (AR-LBD).

documents.title: PARP1 and PD-L1 dual-targeted bifunctional small-molecule inhibitors: a novel strategy for dual immunotherapy of triple-negative breast cancer.
documents.abstract: Current single-agent PD-L1 immunotherapy and PARP inhibitor combination regimens have several drawbacks, including limited response rates, mismatched pharmacokinetics, and overlapping toxicities. This research aims to discover novel bifunctional small molecules that simultaneously block the PD-1/PD-L1 axis and PARP1, with prominent selectivity for PARP subtypes, to overcome bottlenecks in triple-negative breast cancer immunotherapy.

documents.title: Multitarget docking and toxicity-guided prioritisation of phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against wheat fungal pathogens.
documents.abstract: The rising issue of fungicide resistance, along with environmental concerns related to synthetic fungicides, highlights the need for safer and more sustainable antifungal agents. In this computational study, we screened nineteen phytochemicals from locally available medicinal plants in Bangladesh against three fungal protein targets associated with major wheat diseases: class I sesquiterpene synthase (PDB ID: 8H4P) and trichothecene 3-O-acetyltransferase (TRI101; PDB ID: 3B2S) from Fusarium graminearum, and the AvrSr50 effector protein (PDB ID: 7MQQ) from Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici. documents.title: An OGE-HPLC-ABTS-Q-TOF MS Screening of Antioxidant Components in Gushuning Tablet (GSN) With Computational Prediction of Related Biological Targets.
documents.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a severe skeletal disorder that poses a major threat to public health, and oxidative stress may be one of its core pathological mechanisms. The Traditional Chinese Medicine compound preparation Gushuning Tablet (GSN) has been reported to show potential clinical benefits in OP, potentially related to the modulation of OP-associated oxidative stress. However, its antioxidant active material basis and mechanism of action remain unclear. This study aimed to establish an online gradient extraction (OGE)-high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-2,2'-azinobis-(3-ethylbenzthi

documents.title: Identification of novel compounds from Olea Europaea targeting hDus2 as potential anticancer agents: a molecular docking and molecular dynamics study.
documents.abstract: Leukemia, a type of blood cancer, ranks among the top causes of cancer-related fatalities. Human tRNA-dihydrouridine synthase 2 (hDus2) catalyzes the conversion of uridine to dihydrouridine in the tRNA and is overexpressed in cancer cells, facilitating the translational process required for cancer cell growth. Inhibition of hDus2 reduces cancer cell growth and viability while increasing apoptosis sensitivity under stress, making it an excellent cancer target. documents.title: SLC38A2-Driven Glutamine Metabolic Reprogramming Promotes Hypoxic Survival in Glioblastoma.
documents.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is highly refractory to standard therapies, including anti-angiogenic agents such as bevacizumab. While bevacizumab prunes tumor vasculature, it exacerbates intratumoral hypoxia, which drives a metabolically resilient phenotype that limits survival benefits. This study aimed to identify the metabolic dependencies underlying GBM adaptation to hypoxia and to evaluate whether targeting these dependencies could enhance the antitumor efficacy of bevacizumab. Methods: We analyzed the spatial distribution of key metabolites in GBM patients and orthotopic xenograft mouse

documents.title: Advances in injectable liposome-microspheres platforms for osteoarthritis therapy: from sustained delivery to multifunctional disease modification.
documents.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, whole-joint disorder marked by progressive cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodeling, synovial inflammation, and capsular fibrosis, affecting over 500 million individuals worldwide. Current pharmacotherapies are mainly palliative, with no approved disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs (DMOADs). Intra-articular (IA) injection provides direct joint access but is hampered by rapid drug clearance and short residence times. Injectable liposome-microsphere (iLMP) systems have recently emerged as integrative delivery platforms that synergistically combine t

documents.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
documents.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twent

documents.title: Infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TiO2 nanotube surfaces: mechanisms and synergistic design strategies.
documents.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) fabricated via anodization have emerged as a versatile platform for surface modification of orthopedic and dental implants, owing to their tunable nanotopography and excellent potential for multifunctional biofunctionalization. However, the concurrent challenges of implant-associated bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration remain formidable obstacles in clinical practice.
